confirmed.title: Typing in a removed field writes its text into another field with the same name: changing one cart quantity to 0 also empties the next item
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:1733 (fieldList calls liveField(ref) with sync on) and src/content/index.ts:2638-2651 (liveField adopts a field with the same name and type, then proxy.focus and proxy.setValue)
confirmed.evidence: New fixture fx/r8int-cartzero.html?v=labels. It has two text quantity fields, both named qty, labelled 'Quantity of Rye loaf' and 'Quantity of Seeded rye'. Typing 0 removes that row, as an autosaving basket does. In Sift, I cleared the first quantity and typed 0. The page log is row1=, row1=0, focus@row2, input@row2, row2=0, and both items are gone (Total $0.00). The original logs only row1=0 and keeps Seeded rye ($8.00). The pre-round-7 build (scratchpad/ctl on port 9467+10) also keeps Seeded rye and focuses its field. No key was pressed after the 0. On the next run, fieldList() still sees Sift's old field focused. liveField finds exactly one visible input named qty. The removed input has no form any more, so any form matches. liveField adopts that input, sends it focus, and copies Sift's value into it.
confirmed.repro: Start the test Chrome. Run SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r8int/cartzero.ts sift '?v=labels'. It prints rows [] and log row1=, row1=0, row2=0. Run it with 'orig' as the first argument and it prints rows [row2:1]. By hand: open http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r8int-cartzero.html?v=labels, click the first Quantity in Sift, press End, Backspace, type 0, wait 2 s.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The F751 change resolves the field in fieldList with liveField(a.dataset.ref). The default sync=true runs on every extraction and every refreshList, not only on the user's own keystroke. The skeptic's lead was liveField(ref, false). Even then, a swap should be adopted only when the old field was replaced in place (same form, same parent position, or the page focused the new one), never just because one same-named field is left.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 2 of 2 times on fx/r8int-cartzero.html?v=labels. Sift's log was row1=, row1=0, row2=0, rows [] and Total $0.00. The original kept row2 ($8.00). I traced it with capture listeners on the page: focus@row2* then input@row2*=0, both synthetic, which is liveField's proxy.focus plus setValue. The labels differ in this variant, so twinOf's label match cannot fire and this is not the carry path. The pre-round-7 build (ctl on port 9477) kept row2 with no event on it, so this is a regression. The code agrees: fieldList now calls liveField(a.dataset.ref) with sync on, where ctl called elOf. The detached input has no form, so `form === undefined` lets any same-named field match.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts fieldList (~1733): look up the field with elOf, or at least liveField(ref, false). In liveField, when the old field has no form left (form === undefined), never adopt on name and type alone. Require positive evidence of an in-place swap, such as the page focusing the new field (the sift-focus path), and only proxy.focus or setValue from the user's own focus or input handlers.

confirmed.title: After an edit removes the focused field, Sift's focus repair types the same text into another field with the same label (cart quantities, number or text)
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:277-292 (twinOf falls back to any control with the same label) and src/content/index.ts:296-304 (carry writes the typed value and dispatches input)
confirmed.evidence: fx/r8int-cartzero.html has two fields labelled 'Quantity', typed text or (?v=number) number, as in most carts. Typing 0 in the first removes its row. Sift: rows [], log row1=, row1=0, row2=0, Total $0.00. The trace shows input@row2 without focus@row2, so this is the carry path, not liveField. ?v=names (different names) gives the same. The pre-round-7 build gives the same for the default, ?v=names and ?v=number variants, so this is older than round 7. The original removes only Rye loaf (rows [row2:1], $8.00). When paint() finds the focused field gone, refocus() asks twinOf(). The ref is gone, so twinOf() matches any control with the same label: the next item's Quantity. carry() then puts the old field's value there and fires input, because lastTyped > store.actAt. That sends the 0 to the page.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r8int/cartzero.ts sift '?v=number' prints rows []. Add 'orig' as the first argument for the original, which prints rows [row2:1].
confirmed.suspectedCause: carry() is meant for the same field after a re-render. It should only write when the twin stands for the same page element (same data-ref, or one adopted under the rules for a replaced field). A label-only twin may take focus but must never take the typed text.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on ?v=names, ?v=number and the default variant: rows [] and row2=0 each time. In ?v=names and ?v=number the trace shows input@row2*=0 with no focus@row2, and the names differ, so liveField cannot match. At t+100 ms Sift had r5=0 focused. At t+400 ms Sift's r7 (the other 'Quantity') was focused with value 0, and the page's row2 had received it. That is refocusNow, then twinOf's label fallback, then carry() writing spot.value and dispatching input. The ctl build gave the same result for names, number and default, so this is older than round 7. The original removes only Rye loaf (rows [row2:1], $8.00) in all variants.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts carry() (~296): write the value and dispatch input only when twin.dataset.ref === spot.ref (or the ref was legitimately adopted). A label-only twin from twinOf may take focus and the caret, never the typed text.

confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts H.input (~2970-2975): leave SEARCH_FIELD out of the typedRun schedule(0) and suggestAt triggers, or keep it only when lastDur is small. Search boxes whose lists Sift reads via fieldPanel are already refreshed by refreshList on the page's own mutation.

confirmed.title: Escape in a plain search field does not close the suggestion list Sift shows under it (Wikipedia portal)
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:966-980 (escapeList hides Sift's list only once the page hides its own)
confirmed.evidence: www.wikipedia.org, Sift's 'Search Wikipedia' field: type 'Pumper' and Sift shows 6 suggestions. Press Escape: 3 of 3 runs still show 6 suggestions 1.5 s later, focus stays in the field, and the page dropdown is still there. On the original, Escape clears the box and the dropdown is removed. The portal has no Escape handler and relies on the browser's own Escape clearing a type=search box. Sift prevents that default and sends a synthetic Escape, which has no default action. confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts escapeList (~966-980): if the page's list is still visible after a short delay (the existing setTimeout), add the key to store.dismissed (and dismissedRefs) anyway for fieldPanel/fieldList lists ('fp:'/'fl:' keys). confirmed.title: Search results shown under the field after Enter (Discourse) vanish when the page changes while the user arrows through them, and focus is thrown back to the field
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:1729-1743 (fieldList: `a` is swapped for suggestAnchor() when focus is in the sheet, then the post-action branch requires a === shadow.activeElement)
confirmed.evidence: users.rust-lang.org/latest. Search, type 'lifetime', Enter: Sift shows 6 results in its list under the field. ArrowDown puts focus on 'Lifetime issue - expected lifetime…'. Then a page change (I appended 3 divs to body; on a live forum a new-topic update does the same) triggers one routine run (runs 20 to 21). The list is gone and focus is back in the field ('input lifetime'). With focus in the list, `a` is the field, not shadow.activeElement, so fieldList returns undefined. The extractor does not find the Discourse menu on its own. Tab into the list goes the same way, because wrapTab now sends Tab from the field into a popup with tab stops.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-7; SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun scripts/act.ts goto:https://users.rust-lang.org/latest wait:8000 click:Search wait:1500 'type:input[type=search]=>lifetime' wait:3000 press:Enter wait:5000 press:ArrowDown wait:500 "eval:(()=>{for(let i=0;i<3;i++)document.body.appendChild(document.createElement('div'));return 1})()" wait:9000 "eval:[!!document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('.sheet'), document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.activeElement.localName]" prints [false,"input"]. Without the eval step the list stays.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The 'still in it' test should also accept focus inside the field's own suggestion sheet: compare the original shadow.activeElement (before the suggestAnchor() swap) against '.sheet.suggest', not `a`.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 3 of 3 times on users.rust-lang.org/latest. After Search, typing 'lifetime' and Enter, Sift shows 6 results under the field. ArrowDown focuses 'Lifetime issue - expected lifetime…'. After a page mutation (3 divs appended), one routine run fires (runs 20 to 21). Sift's sheet is then gone and focus is back in the input. The page's own .search-menu results are still visible with 6 links, so Sift differs from the original. With no mutation, the list and focus stayed for 9 s. The code agrees: in fieldList, `a` is swapped for suggestAnchor() when focus is in the sheet, so `a === shadow.activeElement` is false in the post-action branch and it returns undefined. The trigger was synthetic, but routine mutations (relative times, message-bus updates) do this on a live forum.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts fieldList (~1729-1743): keep the original shadow.activeElement and treat focus inside '.sheet.suggest' as being at the field. Use `(a === shadow.activeElement || shadow.activeElement?.closest('.sheet.suggest'))` in the panel condition instead of `a === shadow.activeElement`.

confirmed.title: HN Search: about 1 in 4 results shows the raw URL as the headline and the real title as a small link
confirmed.evidence: 7 of 30 Sift items have a headline that is the URL in parentheses, e.g. '(https://fasterthanli.me/articles/a-half-hour-to-learn-rust)' in bold, then 'A half-hour to learn Rust · 1444 points | selvan | 6 years ago' below. Others: '(http://blog.rust-lang.org/2015/05/15/Rust-1.0.html)' over 'Announcing Rust 1.0', and windows-rs, 'why-i-left-rust', and more. Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-4/research/shots/r8t4-hns-rust.png (items 3 and 4)
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9464 SIFT_TAB=T4-generic bun scripts/act.ts "goto:https://hn.algolia.com/?q=rust" wait:6000 "eval:(()=>{const li=[...document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('li.item')];return [li.length, li.filter(l=>/^\(https?:/.test(l.querySelector('a')?.innerText||'')).length]})()" prints [30,7].
confirmed.suspectedCause: Unverified. The item-title choice in src/content/extract/generic.ts seems to prefer the longer link text when the real title is short, and then demotes the title link into the meta line.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, 30 items and 7 of them with a URL headline, as claimed. Item 3 is '(https://fasterthanli.me/articles/a-half-hour-to-learn-rust)' in bold, with 'A half-hour to learn Rust · 1444 points…' as a small link under it. Item 4 is '(http://blog.rust-lang.org/2015/05/15/Rust-1.0.html)' over 'Announcing Rust 1.0'. The original's .Story_title markup is the same for every story: a[href=item?id] with the title, then a.Story_link with '(url)'. Cause: titleLink() counts a link as a title when its text is at least 70% of its line. For the URL link, the line includes the title link, so a URL at least about 2.3 times as long as the title passes. Discord's 77-character URL against its 40-character title fails, and the half-hour one passes. toItem() then sorts the named links by length, so the URL wins. This is not new, but it puts the wrong headline on about 1 in 4 search results, more than polish. Medium.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts titleLink(), return false for a link whose whole text is in parentheses '(…)' or is a bare URL. That is the same 'source after a headline' rule side() already applies to the link's neighbors. Another option: in toItem(), drop such links from `named` before the longest-text sort.
